decisions.choice: the Hebrew (Masoretic) text of Jeremiah, which is longer than the Greek and arranges part of the book differently
alternatives: follow the shorter Greek form and its order of chapters
decisions.reason: This translation follows the Hebrew text of Jeremiah throughout. The Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation, gives a form of the book about one-eighth shorter. It lacks many words and phrases and some whole passages (for example 33:14-26 and most of 39:4-13), and it places the oracles against the nations (chapters 46-51 in the Hebrew) in the middle of chapter 25, after 25:13, and in a different order. Hebrew fragments of Jeremiah found at Qumran include both a shorter form close to the Greek and the longer form, so both forms of the book were copied in ancient times. The difference shows even here: the Greek opens "The word of God that came to Jeremiah". Later decisions mention a Greek reading only where it bears on the sense (see 25:13 and 46:1).

decisions.choice: of the priests: Jeremiah came from a priestly family
decisions.reason: The phrase most naturally describes Jeremiah's family, so that he was of priestly descent; it could describe Hilkiah alone, but either way the family was priestly. Jeremiah is never shown serving as a priest. This Hilkiah is probably not the high priest of the same name in Josiah's reign (2 Kings 22:4), who served in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Anathoth: a town of priests in Benjamin, a few miles north-east of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Anathoth was one of the towns given to the priests in the territory of Benjamin (Joshua 21:18). Solomon sent the priest Abiathar home there in disgrace (1 Kings 2:26). Jeremiah later bought a field there (32:7-9), and men of his own town plotted against him (11:21-23).

decisions.choice: a comma at the end of the verse (Literal, Balanced); separate sentences (Readable)
decisions.reason: Verses 1-3 are one Hebrew sentence, the heading of the book. Literal and Balanced keep it as one sentence running into verses 2 and 3. Readable breaks it into short sentences and supplies "These are", "came from a family of" and "the town of" to make the heading plain.

decisions.choice: "Jeremías hijo de Hilcías", "Anatot"
decisions.reason: The names in the forms already published in Spanish (Matthew 2:17; 2 Kings 22:12; Anatot in Joshua and Chronicles), as the Isaiah-Jeremiah-Ezra terms note sets.

decisions.choice: Yeremia, Hilkia, Anathothi, Benyamini
decisions.reason: The names in the forms of the published books (1 Chronicles 3:15; 1 Kings 2:26; 1 Chronicles 6:45) and of the terms note for Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: "Jérémie fils de Hilqiya", "Anatoth", for the whole book
decisions.reason: The usual French form of the prophet's name; Hilqiya and Anatoth follow the forms already published in Kings and Chronicles (2 Kings 22:4; 1 Chronicles 6:45).

decisions.choice: "Giê-rê-mi con trai Hinh-kia", "A-na-tốt"
decisions.reason: The names as already published (Matthew 2:17; 2 Chronicles 36:12; 1 Kings 2:26) and settled in the terms note for the whole book. Literal and Balanced keep verses 1-3 as one heading running on with commas, as the English does.

decisions.choice: each verse of the heading (1:1-3) closes as its own sentence
alternatives: one sentence running across verses 1-3, as the English Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: Korean puts the verb at the end, so a relative clause running from verse 1 into verses 2 and 3 cannot keep each verse's words after its own marker. Each verse is closed with its own verb, and verse 2 picks up "him" (그에게) to keep the link.

decisions.choice: Jeremias, filho de Hilquias; Anatote; Benjamim
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the prophet is "Jeremias", the form Matthew 2:17 and 16:14 give him in Portuguese, and "filho de" stands between commas, as Isaiah 1:1 names "Isaías, filho de Amoz". The town is "Anatote", as 1 Kings 2:26 has it in Portuguese; the names of 2 Kings 22-25 (Josias, Jeoaquim, Zedequias, Joaquim, Nabucodonosor, Gedalias, Nebuzaradã) are kept through the book.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic of this chapter
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader setting that capitalises pronouns referring to God has nothing to change in Amharic; the English spans in this chapter (from verse 2) have no Amharic counterpart.

decisions.choice: यिर्मयाह, हिल्किय्याह, अनातोत, बिन्यामीन
decisions.reason: The prophet's name is यिर्मयाह, the New Testament's form (Matthew 2:17; 16:14). His father's name is हिल्किय्याह, the form 2 Kings 18:18 and 22-23 use for others of that name, and Anathoth is अनातोत, as Joshua 21:18 and 1 Kings 2:26. Book-wide choice for Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: a comma at the end of the verse (Literal, Balanced); separate sentences (Readable)
decisions.reason: Verses 1-3 are one Hebrew sentence, the heading of the book. Literal and Balanced keep it as one sentence running into verses 2 and 3 with relative clauses (जो, जिसके पास), as the English does; Readable breaks it up.

decisions.choice: Иеремия, сын Хелкии; Анафоф
decisions.reason: The traditional Russian forms: Иеремия as in Matthew 2:17 and 16:14 in this translation, Хелкия as in 2 Kings 18:18, Анафоф as in 1 Kings 2:26. One form each through the book.

decisions.choice: в земле племени Вениамина
decisions.reason: Readable says племя for the tribe, as the Pentateuch note has it for Readable (колено at Literal and Balanced); here only Readable names the tribe.

decisions.choice: Book-wide register for Jeremiah, following the prophetic conventions set for Isaiah: the oracles (verse, and prose oracles) are plain style (だ・である) at every level, Readable too; the narrative and the prose sermons as narration are plain at Literal and Balanced and です・ます at Readable, with light respect forms for the LORD only; Jeremiah narrates himself as "わたし"; God speaks plainly and never uses a respect form of himself.
alternatives: です・ます in the oracles at Readable
decisions.reason: The same register rules as Isaiah and Hosea, so the prophets read alike; see notes/JER-JER-1.md, JEREMIAH CONVENTIONS.

decisions.choice: Names as in 2 Kings and 1 Kings: "ヒルキヤの子エレミヤ" (L, B), "ヒルキヤの息子エレミヤ" (R); "アナトト" (R "アナトトの町", 1 Kings 2:26); "ベニヤミン".
decisions.reason: Jeremiah is エレミヤ as in Matthew 2:17 and 2 Chronicles 35:25; Hilkiah and Anathoth keep the forms of the historical books.

decisions.choice: the word of Yahweh came to him: Yahweh gave him his message
decisions.reason: The phrase, common in Jeremiah, presents the prophet's message as given to him by God, not thought up by him (compare verse 4; 2 Samuel 7:4; Hosea 1:1). "The word" here is the message as a whole.

decisions.choice: the thirteenth year of Josiah: about 627 BC
decisions.reason: Josiah reigned thirty-one years (2 Kings 22:1). His thirteenth year was about 627 BC, five years before the book of the law was found in the temple in his eighteenth year (2 Kings 22:3-8). Jeremiah himself counts his years of preaching from this year (25:3).

decisions.choice: began to give his messages
decisions.reason: Readable says "began" because verse 3 goes on to say how long the messages continued.

decisions.choice: during the reign of ... in the thirteenth year of Josiah's reign (Balanced); while ... was king ... thirteenth year as king (Readable)
decisions.reason: This is the book-wide wording for the dated headings of Jeremiah ("in the days of", "in the Nth year of"). Verse 3 and the later headings use it too.

decisions.choice: "en los días de" / "en el año trece de su reinado" (L); "durante el reinado de" (B); "cuando ... era rey" (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording of Jeremiah's dated headings at each level, following the English levels; verse 3 and the later headings keep it.

decisions.choice: katika siku za X (Literal); wakati wa utawala wa X (Balanced); wakati X alipokuwa mfalme (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording of Jeremiah's dated headings in Swahili, following the three English levels; "mwaka wa N wa utawala wa X" (Balanced) and "mwaka wa N wa X kuwa mfalme" (Readable) for the year.

decisions.choice: "le SEIGNEUR" for YHWH, in capitals, for the whole book
decisions.reason: As in the Pentateuch, Kings and the Psalms: "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals matches the English "the LORD", with "Yahvé" as the setting's alternative; "l’Éternel", the Segond tradition, is the form a reviewer may prefer.

decisions.choice: "sous le règne de X ... la Ne année du règne de X" (B); "quand X était roi ... la Ne année où X était roi" (R), for the book's dated headings
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for Jeremiah's dated headings, following the English Balanced and Readable; Literal keeps "aux jours de", "la Ne année de son règne".

decisions.choice: "dưới triều X ... năm thứ N X trị vì" (Balanced); "khi X làm vua ... năm thứ N X làm vua" (Readable)
alternatives: "trong những ngày của X" at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for Jeremiah's dated headings at each level, following the English pattern; Literal keeps "trong những ngày của". Used again in verse 3 and the later headings.

decisions.choice: 요시야의 시대 ... 제13년 (Literal); 요시야가 다스리던 때 ... 다스린 지 13년째 되는 해 (Balanced); 요시야가 유다 왕이었을 때 ... 왕이 된 지 13년째 되는 해 (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for Jeremiah's dated headings, following the Kings formula; years are in figures at every level. Later headings use the same wording.

decisions.choice: nos dias de X, no Nº ano do seu reinado (L); durante o reinado de X, no Nº ano do reinado de X (B); quando X era rei, no Nº ano em que X era rei (R)
alternatives: no Nº ano de X como rei
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the dated headings of Jeremiah keep one wording at each level, as the English does (r-en-2). Literal keeps the Hebrew's "nos dias de"; Balanced says "durante o reinado de"; Readable says "quando X era rei" and "no Nº ano em que X era rei", the plain shape 2 Kings 25:8 uses in Readable Portuguese. Verse 3 and the later headings (25:1; 26:1; 27:1; 32:1; 36:1 and after) repeat it.

decisions.choice: a palavra do SENHOR veio a
alternatives: a palavra do SENHOR foi dirigida a
decisions.reason: "Veio", the plain verb of the Hebrew, as 1 Kings 17:2 and 2 Kings 20:4 have the phrase in Portuguese; Readable turns it into God giving his message (m1), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: प्रभु for both YHWH and Adonai; the divine_name setting tells them apart
decisions.reason: Hindi प्रभु translates both the divine name YHWH and the title Adonai ("Lord", 1:6). Wherever the Hebrew has the name, प्रभु (or परमेश्वर after the title प्रभु, in "the Lord GOD") stands inside a divine_name span whose alternative is याहवे, so a reader who switches the setting sees which is which; where प्रभु stands alone it is Adonai. यहोवा is not used.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Hindi
decisions.reason: The English marks God's pronouns ("his", "my", "me") with the deity_pronoun setting. Devanagari has no capital letters, so the Hindi has no such spans; respect for God is carried by the honorific third person (वे, उनका, उन्होंने). This holds for every record of this file.

decisions.choice: X के शासनकाल में ... X के राज्य के Nवें वर्ष में (Balanced); जब X ... राजा था ... X के राजा होने का Nवाँ वर्ष (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for Jeremiah's dated headings ("in the days of", "in the Nth year of"), following the English decision. Literal keeps "के दिनों में" and "के राज्य के Nवें वर्ष में". The king's names keep the forms of 2 Kings 21-24: आमोन, योशिय्याह, यहोयाकीम, सिदकिय्याह.

decisions.choice: во дни X, в N-й год его царствования (L); в царствование X (B); когда X был царём (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for Jeremiah's dated headings, as the English levels have one each. Later headings ("in the days of", "in the Nth year of") use the same words.

decisions.choice: The relative "to whom" (1:2) is carried by "その彼に" (L) and by naming Jeremiah (B, R), so 1:1, 1:2 and 1:3 can each be a full Japanese sentence in its own record.
decisions.reason: A Japanese relative clause must come before its noun, which would pull 1:2-3 in front of 1:1.

decisions.choice: Kings as in 2 Kings 21-24: "アモンの子ヨシヤ" (L, B), "アモンの息子ヨシヤ" (R).
decisions.reason: The 2 Kings forms.

en.L: and it came in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the exile of Jerusalem in the fifth month.
en.B: and it came during the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the end of the eleventh year of the reign of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, the year Jerusalem went into exile, in the fifth month.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} kept speaking to Jeremiah while Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah. These messages went on until the end of Zedekiah's eleventh year as king of Judah. Zedekiah was another son of Josiah. In the fifth month of that year, the people of Jerusalem were taken away as captives.

decisions.choice: it came: the word of Yahweh, the subject carried over from verse 2
decisions.reason: The verb has no new subject; it continues "the word of Yahweh came" from verse 2. The heading thus covers Jeremiah's preaching across three reigns.

decisions.choice: Jehoiakim and Zedekiah: the reigns named, and two short reigns left out
decisions.reason: The heading names the three kings whose reigns were long: Josiah, Jehoiakim (609-598 BC) and Zedekiah (597-586 BC), both sons of Josiah. It passes over Jehoahaz and Jehoiachin, who each reigned three months (2 Kings 23:31; 24:8).

decisions.choice: the exile of Jerusalem in the fifth month: the fall of the city in 586 BC
decisions.reason: In the fifth month of Zedekiah's eleventh year the Babylonians burned the temple and took the people of Jerusalem into exile (2 Kings 25:8-11; Jeremiah 52:12-15). Jeremiah went on speaking after this (chapters 40-44); the heading marks the span of his work under Judah's last kings.

decisions.choice: kept speaking ... These messages went on (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the same word of the LORD went on coming to Jeremiah (see m1), and says in a separate sentence that Zedekiah was another son of Josiah. Balanced keeps "it came" and uses the heading wording of verse 2.

decisions.choice: "Joacim", "Sedequías", "destierro"

decisions.choice: to me: the book now speaks in Jeremiah's own voice
decisions.reason: After the heading in the third person (verses 1-3), Jeremiah tells of his call himself. The same first-person telling runs through the visions of verses 11-19.

decisions.choice: came to me, saying: (Literal); came to me: (Balanced); gave me this message: (Readable)
decisions.reason: This formula returns many times in Jeremiah, and each level keeps one wording for it throughout the book.

decisions.choice: "Vino a mí la palabra del SEÑOR, diciendo:" (L); "La palabra del SEÑOR vino a mí:" (B); "El SEÑOR me dio este mensaje:" (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as the terms note sets it for Spanish, kept the same at each level throughout Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: Neno la BWANA likanijia, kusema: (Literal); Neno la BWANA likanijia: (Balanced); BWANA alinipa ujumbe huu: (Readable)
decisions.reason: The formula returns throughout Jeremiah, and each level keeps this one wording for it, as the terms note sets it (Literal as 1 Chronicles 22:8). The narrative "-ka-" carries the Hebrew "and".

decisions.choice: "La parole du SEIGNEUR me fut adressée, disant :" (L); "La parole du SEIGNEUR me fut adressée :" (B); "Le SEIGNEUR m’a donné ce message :" (R), for the whole book
decisions.reason: The formula returns many times in Jeremiah; each level keeps one wording, built on the Kings formula "la parole du SEIGNEUR fut adressée à X".

decisions.choice: passé simple for Jeremiah's own narration at L and B ("me fut adressée", "je dis"); passé composé at R ("j’ai répondu")
decisions.reason: Jeremiah tells of his call and his visions in the first person. French written narrative uses the passé simple, Readable the passé composé, as in Kings and in John's narration in Revelation. The oracles themselves are speech and never take the passé simple.

decisions.choice: "Lời của CHÚA đến với tôi rằng:" (Literal); "Lời CHÚA đến với tôi:" (Balanced); "CHÚA ban cho tôi sứ điệp này:" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The terms note's wording for this formula, kept at each level through the book, built on Kings' "lời CHÚA đến với X".

decisions.choice: 주의 말씀이 나에게 임하여 말씀하셨다 (Literal); 주의 말씀이 나에게 임했다 (Balanced); 주께서 나에게 이 말씀을 주셨다 (Readable)
decisions.reason: The formula returns throughout Jeremiah and each level keeps one wording for it, as 1 Chronicles 22:8. It ends with a period, not the English colon, and the speech follows in quotation marks.

decisions.choice: E a palavra do SENHOR veio a mim, dizendo: (L); A palavra do SENHOR veio a mim: (B); O SENHOR me deu esta mensagem: (R)
alternatives: A palavra do SENHOR me foi dirigida
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the formula that opens so many of Jeremiah's messages keeps one wording at each level, as the English does (r-en-1). Literal keeps "dizendo:"; Balanced drops it, as Portuguese introduces speech with the colon alone; Readable says that God gave the message, as the English Readable does. With "a Jeremias" in place of "a mim" it serves the third-person headings too (7:1; 11:1 and after: "A palavra que veio a Jeremias da parte do SENHOR").

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ቃል ወደ እኔ መጣ፤ እንዲህም አለ፦" (Literal); "... ቃል ወደ እኔ መጣ፦" (Balanced); "{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ይህን መልእክት ሰጠኝ፦" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The formula that opens Jeremiah's messages is given one wording through the book, as Kings and Chronicles give "the word of the LORD came to X": Literal keeps "saying" as "እንዲህም አለ" before the speech mark; Readable follows the English "gave me this message".

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} का वचन X के पास पहुँचा (L, B); {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने X को यह संदेश दिया (R)
decisions.reason: The formula "the word of the LORD came to X" has one wording per level through the Prophets, as the terms note sets it and as Isaiah 38:4 and 1 Kings have it. Literal does not translate "saying" (le'mor) as a separate word: the colon introduces the words, as Isaiah 38:4. Book-wide choice.

decisions.choice: И было слово ГОСПОДА ко мне, говоря: (L); ГОСПОДЬ обратился ко мне: (B); ГОСПОДЬ дал мне такое слово: (R)

decisions.choice: The word-event formula, the same through Jeremiah: wayhi devar YHWH 'elai lemor "{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の言葉がわたしに臨んで言った" (L), "{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の言葉がわたしに臨んだ" (B), "{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は、わたしに次のように語られました" (R); with "a second time" "再び" (L, B), "二度目に" (R).

records.literal_gloss: Before I formed you in the belly I knew you, and before you came out from [the] womb I consecrated you; a prophet to the nations I gave you.

en.L: "Before I formed you in the belly I knew you, \q and before you came out from the womb I consecrated you; \q a prophet to the nations I appointed you."
en.B: "I knew you before I shaped you in the womb; \q I set you apart before you came out of the womb; \q I have given you to the nations as a prophet."
en.R: "I knew you before I formed your body inside your mother. \q Before you were born, I chose you for a holy task. \q I made you a prophet to the nations."

es.L: «Antes que te formara en el vientre te conocí, \q y antes que salieras del seno materno te consagré; \q profeta a las naciones te puse».
es.B: «Te conocí antes de formarte en el vientre; \q te aparté antes de que salieras del seno materno; \q te he dado a las naciones como profeta».
es.R: «Te conocí antes de formar tu cuerpo dentro de tu madre. \q Antes de que nacieras, te elegí para una tarea santa. \q Te hice profeta para las naciones».

fr.L: « Avant que je te forme dans le ventre, je t’ai connu, \q et avant que tu sortes du sein, je t’ai consacré ; \q prophète pour les nations, je t’ai établi. »

vi.L: "Trước khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nắn nên ngươi trong bụng [mẹ], {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã biết ngươi, \q và trước khi ngươi ra khỏi lòng mẹ, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã biệt riêng ngươi ra thánh; \q Ta đã lập ngươi làm nhà tiên tri cho các dân tộc."

vi.R: "Ta đã biết con trước khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tạo nên thân thể con trong lòng mẹ. \q Trước khi con chào đời, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã chọn con cho một công việc thánh. \q Ta đã lập con làm nhà tiên tri cho các dân tộc."

ko.L: "배 속에서 너를 빚기 전에 내가 너를 알았고, \q 네가 태에서 나오기 전에 내가 너를 거룩하게 구별했다. \q 민족들의 예언자로 내가 너를 주었다."

hi.L: "गर्भ में तुम्हें रचने से पहले मैंने तुम्हें जाना, \q और कोख से तुम्हारे निकलने से पहले मैंने तुम्हें पवित्र किया; \q जातियों के लिए भविष्यद्वक्ता मैंने तुम्हें ठहराया।"

hi.R: "तुम्हारी माँ के गर्भ में तुम्हारा शरीर बनाने से पहले ही मैं तुम्हें जानता था। \q तुम्हारे जन्म से पहले ही मैंने तुम्हें एक पवित्र काम के लिए चुन लिया। \q मैंने तुम्हें देशों के लिए नबी ठहराया।"

ru.L: «Прежде чем {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} образовал тебя во чреве, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} знал тебя, \q и прежде чем ты вышел из утробы, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} освятил тебя; \q пророком для народов {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} поставил тебя.»
ru.B: «Я знал тебя прежде, чем создал тебя в утробе; \q {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} посвятил тебя прежде, чем ты вышел из утробы; \q {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} дал тебя народам пророком.»
ru.R: «Я знал тебя ещё до того, как создал твоё тело в утробе матери. \q Ещё до твоего рождения {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} избрал тебя для святого дела. \q Я сделал тебя пророком для народов.»

ja.L: 胎の内にあなたを形づくる前から、わたしはあなたを知っていた。 \q あなたが胎から出る前に、わたしはあなたを聖別した。 \q 国々への預言者として、わたしはあなたを立てた。
ja.B: わたしは、胎の内にあなたを形づくる前から、あなたを知っていた。 \q あなたが胎から出て来る前に、あなたをわたしのものとして取り分けた。 \q わたしはあなたを、国々のための預言者とした。
ja.R: わたしは、母親のおなかの中であなたの体を形づくる前から、あなたを知っていた。 \q あなたが生まれる前に、わたしはあなたを選び、聖なる務めに就かせることにした。 \q わたしはあなたを、国々に語る預言者にしたのだ。

decisions.choice: I knew you: I chose you and took you as my own
decisions.reason: To "know" someone in Hebrew can mean to choose him and bind him to oneself (Genesis 18:19; Amos 3:2). God's knowing Jeremiah came before Jeremiah was formed, so it rests on God's choice, not on anything Jeremiah had done.

decisions.choice: I formed you in the belly: God shaping a person, as a potter shapes clay
decisions.reason: The verb is the potter's word (18:4-6) and the word for God forming the first man (Genesis 2:7). The servant in Isaiah is also called and formed from the womb (Isaiah 49:1, 5), and Paul speaks of his own call in the same terms (Galatians 1:15).

decisions.choice: I consecrated you: set you apart as holy for my service
decisions.reason: The verb is used for setting apart priests and holy things for God (Exodus 28:41; 29:44). Jeremiah, of a priestly family (verse 1), is set apart for another service, as a prophet.

decisions.choice: a prophet to the nations I gave you: appointed you as a prophet whose word reaches the nations
decisions.reason: The verb is "give", used here as "appoint, make" (as in verse 18). Jeremiah's message concerns not Judah alone but other nations too (verse 10; 25:15-38; chapters 46-51).

decisions.choice: set you apart (Balanced); chose you for a holy task (Readable); given you to the nations as a prophet (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "consecrated". Balanced and Readable say what consecrating means for a person. Balanced keeps the verb "give" of the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: verses 5 and 10 and the speech of verses 15-19 set in lines
decisions.reason: These words of God have the balanced, parallel lines of Hebrew verse, and the accents divide them as verse. They are set in lines inside the prose account of the call; the story around them stays prose.

decisions.choice: "te consagré" (L); "te aparté" (B); "te elegí para una tarea santa" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "consagrar"; Balanced and Readable say what consecrating means for a person, as the English levels do.

decisions.choice: kukuunda
decisions.reason: "-unda" is the verb for shaping or building something, close to the potter's verb of the Hebrew (meaning decision m2); Readable uses the common "kuumba", to create.

decisions.choice: nilikuweka wakfu (Literal); nilikutenga (Balanced); nilikuchagua kwa kazi takatifu (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the language of setting apart priests and holy things; Balanced and Readable say what it means for a person, as the English levels do.

decisions.choice: God's words in verses 5, 10 and 15-19 set in lines and in « »
decisions.reason: The call is told as a narrative, so God's speech to Jeremiah takes French quotation marks, as the English quotes it; its parallel lines follow the English and the Hebrew's division.

decisions.choice: "je t’ai mis à part" (B); "je t’ai choisi pour une mission sainte" (R); "je t’ai consacré" (L)
decisions.reason: As the English, Balanced and Readable say what consecrating a person means (m3).

decisions.choice: God says "Ta" and calls Jeremiah "ngươi" (Literal), "con" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The terms note's address for God speaking to one person, as he speaks to Hezekiah in 2 Kings 19:20 and 20:5: "ngươi" keeps the Literal formal, "con" gives the warmth of a call. Jeremiah answers with "con" for himself (verse 6). "Ta" is spanned only in mid-sentence.

decisions.choice: "Ta đã ban con làm nhà tiên tri"
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the Hebrew verb "give", as the English Balanced does; Literal and Readable say "lập" (appoint).

decisions.choice: God speaks in 해라체 with 나 and 너, and never uses the honorific -시- of himself
decisions.reason: As in the earlier books and the Korean terms note, God speaks in the plain 해라체 throughout Jeremiah and names himself without -시- (주가 말한다), while the narrator and the prophet speak about him with -시-.

decisions.choice: tu (God to Jeremiah)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: God speaks to Jeremiah with "tu" at every level, as he speaks to one person through the Old Testament and to Isaiah (Isaiah 6:9); Jeremiah answers him with "tu" too (verse 6; the laments of 11-20). Kings, officials and the people speak to Jeremiah with "você".

decisions.choice: modelar (L, B); formar (R); estabeleci (L), entreguei às nações como profeta (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is the potter's word (m2), so Literal and Balanced say "modelar", the verb for shaping clay, and Readable the plain "formar o teu corpo". The verse is well known in Portuguese in wording this translation does not copy; each line is drafted from the Hebrew, keeping its order at Literal, with "estabeleci" for the verb "give" used as "appoint" (m4).

decisions.choice: "ቀደስኩህ" (Literal); "ለየሁህ" (Balanced); "ለሕዝቦች" for "to the nations" at every level
decisions.reason: God speaks to Jeremiah with the familiar "አንተ", and Jeremiah answers with "አንተ", as everywhere in prayer. Balanced "ለየሁህ" (set apart) is the verb the Amharic Galatians 1:15 uses where Paul echoes this verse ("ለይቶ"), though that is an echo, not a quotation. The nations (goyim) are "ሕዝቦች", as in the Old Testament on main; "አሕዛብ" is kept for New Testament quotations.

decisions.choice: God says तुम to Jeremiah; Jeremiah says तू to God
decisions.reason: As everywhere in this translation, तू is used only in speech to God (1:6); God speaking to the prophet, to Israel, to Jerusalem or to anyone else uses तुम. Book-wide choice for Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: भविष्यद्वक्ता (L, B), नबी (R); जातियाँ (L), देश (B, R)
decisions.reason: Prophet is भविष्यद्वक्ता at Literal and Balanced and नबी at Readable, as the New Testament and the history books have it. The nations (goyim) are जातियाँ at Literal and देश at Balanced and Readable, where जाति would also suggest caste, as the poetry note sets it.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on God's "I" inside a sentence
decisions.reason: English capitalises "I" anyway and has no span on it; Russian writes я in lower case, so God's я inside a sentence takes the deity_pronoun span, like меня and мне. A sentence-initial Я is written plainly.

decisions.choice: освятил (L); посвятил (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the root of holiness; Balanced says what it means for a person, being set apart for God's service.

decisions.choice: hiqdishtikha "聖別した" (L), "わたしのものとして取り分けた" (B), "選び、聖なる務めに就かせることにした" (R); natattikha "立てた" (L), "とした" (B), "にした" (R).
decisions.reason: 聖別 is the word of Exodus and Leviticus; Balanced and Readable say what it means here (m3).

source.text: וָאֹמַ֗ר אֲהָהּ֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה הִנֵּ֥ה לֹא־יָדַ֖עְתִּי דַּבֵּ֑רכִּי־נַ֖עַר אָנֹֽכִי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And I said, ah, Lord Yahweh, look, not I know to speak, for a youth I [am].

en.L: And I said, "Ah, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! Look, I do not know [how] to speak, for a youth I [am]."
en.B: I said, "Oh, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! I do not know how to speak; I am a mere youth."
en.R: I answered, "Oh no, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! I do not know how to speak well. I am still young."

es.L: Y dije: «¡Ah, Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}! Mira, no sé hablar, porque muchacho [soy]».
es.B: Yo dije: «¡Ay, Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}! No sé hablar; no soy más que un muchacho».
es.R: Yo respondí: «¡Oh no, Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}! No sé hablar bien. Todavía soy muy joven».

fr.L: Et je dis : « Ah ! Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} ! Voici, je ne sais pas parler, car je [suis] un garçon. »
fr.B: Je dis : « Ah ! Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}, je ne sais pas parler : je ne suis qu’un jeune garçon. »
fr.R: J’ai répondu : « Oh non, Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} ! Je ne sais pas bien parler. Je suis encore trop jeune. »

sw.L: Nami nikasema, "Ole wangu, Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}! Tazama, sijui [jinsi ya] kusema, kwa maana mimi [ni] kijana."
sw.B: Nikasema, "Ee Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}! Sijui kusema; mimi ni kijana tu."
sw.R: Nikajibu, "Hapana, Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}! Sijui kusema vizuri. Bado mimi ni kijana."

vi.L: Và tôi nói: "Ôi, lạy Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}! Kìa, con không biết nói, vì con [là] một đứa trẻ."
vi.B: Tôi thưa: "Ôi, lạy Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}! Con không biết ăn nói, vì con chỉ là một đứa trẻ."
vi.R: Tôi đáp: "Ôi, lạy Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}! Con không biết nói cho giỏi. Con còn trẻ quá."

ko.L: 그래서 내가 말했다. "아, 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}! 보십시오, 저는 말할 줄을 모릅니다. 저는 아이입니다."
ko.B: 내가 말했다. "아, 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}! 저는 말할 줄 모릅니다. 저는 아직 어린 젊은이일 뿐입니다."
ko.R: 내가 대답했다. "아, 안 됩니다, 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}! 저는 말을 잘할 줄 모릅니다. 저는 아직 어립니다."

pt.L: E eu disse: "Ah, Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}! Eis que eu não sei falar, pois um rapaz eu [sou]."
pt.B: Eu disse: "Ah, Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}! Eu não sei falar; sou apenas um rapaz."
pt.R: Eu respondi: "Ah, não, Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}! Eu não sei falar bem. Ainda sou muito novo."

am.L: እኔም እንዲህ አልኩ፦ «ወይኔ፣ ጌታ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሆይ! እነሆ፣ መናገር አላውቅም፤ ብላቴና ነኝና።»
am.B: እኔም እንዲህ አልኩ፦ «ወይኔ፣ ጌታ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሆይ! እንዴት እንደምናገር አላውቅም፤ ገና ልጅ ነኝ።»
am.R: እኔም እንዲህ ብዬ መለስኩ፦ «ኧረ ጌታ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሆይ! አሳምሬ መናገር አልችልም። ገና ወጣት ነኝ።»

hi.L: और मैंने कहा, "हाय, प्रभु {{divine_name:परमेश्वर|याहवे}}! देख, मैं बोलना नहीं जानता, क्योंकि मैं लड़का [हूँ]।"
hi.B: मैंने कहा, "हाय, प्रभु {{divine_name:परमेश्वर|याहवे}}! मुझे बोलना नहीं आता; मैं तो अभी लड़का ही हूँ।"
hi.R: मैंने उत्तर दिया, "हाय, प्रभु {{divine_name:परमेश्वर|याहवे}}! मैं ठीक से बोलना नहीं जानता। मैं अभी कम उम्र का हूँ।"

ru.L: И сказал я: «Ах, Владыка {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Яхве}}! Вот, я не умею говорить, потому что юн я.»
ru.B: Я сказал: «О Владыка {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Яхве}}! Я не умею говорить: я ещё слишком молод.»
ru.R: Я ответил: «Ах нет, Владыка {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Яхве}}! Я не умею хорошо говорить. Я ещё молод.»

ja.L: そしてわたしは言った。「ああ、{{divine_name:主なる神|主ヤハウェ}}よ。ご覧ください。わたしは語ることを知りません。わたしは若者ですから。」
ja.B: わたしは言った。「ああ、{{divine_name:主なる神|主ヤハウェ}}よ。わたしはどう語ればよいのか分かりません。まだほんの若者にすぎないのです。」
ja.R: わたしは答えました。「ああ、とても無理です、{{divine_name:主なる神|主ヤハウェ}}よ。わたしはうまく話すことができません。わたしはまだ若いのです。」

decisions.choice: a youth: a boy or young man, not yet of an age to speak with authority
decisions.reason: The word covers a wide range, from a baby (Exodus 2:6) to a young man of fighting age (2 Samuel 18:5). Jeremiah's exact age is not known. The point is that he is too young and untried to be heeded by elders and kings; Solomon says the same of himself (1 Kings 3:7).

decisions.choice: ah: a cry of dismay addressed to God
decisions.reason: The same cry is heard from Joshua (Joshua 7:7), Gideon (Judges 6:22) and Ezekiel (Ezekiel 4:14), each time protesting or fearing before God.

decisions.choice: I do not know how to speak: an objection like that of Moses
decisions.reason: Moses pleaded that he was not a man of words (Exodus 4:10). God answers Jeremiah as he answered Moses, by promising to give him the words (verses 7-9; Exodus 4:11-12).

decisions.choice: Lord GOD
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the title Adonai ("Lord") followed by the divine name. Writing the name as GOD after "Lord" avoids "Lord LORD", as in Isaiah.

decisions.choice: "¡Ah, Señor DIOS!" (L); "¡Ay, Señor DIOS!" (B); "¡Oh no, Señor DIOS!" (R)
decisions.reason: Adonai with the divine name is "Señor DIOS", as the terms notes set; the cry of dismay follows each English level and returns in 4:10 and 14:13.

decisions.choice: Ole wangu (Literal); Ee (Balanced); Hapana (Readable)
decisions.reason: The cry of dismay to God is worded as in the published Judges 6:22 ("Ole wangu, Bwana MUNGU") and Joshua 7:7 ("Ee Bwana MUNGU"); Readable says "No" as the English "Oh no". The same wording returns at 4:10 and 14:13.

decisions.choice: "Seigneur DIEU" for Adonai YHWH, with "DIEU" under the setting
decisions.reason: As in the earlier French books; addressed directly, without the article.

decisions.choice: "un garçon" (L); "un jeune garçon" (B); "trop jeune" (R)
decisions.reason: The word ranges from a baby to a young man (m1). "Enfant" would make him a small child, and "jeune homme" loses the point that he is untried.

decisions.choice: "Ôi, lạy Chúa là CHÚA"
decisions.reason: The terms note's form for "Ah, Lord GOD" (also 4:10): "Ôi" for the cry of dismay, "Chúa là CHÚA" for Adonai YHWH as in Samuel and the Psalms. Jeremiah calls himself "con" before God.

decisions.choice: 주 하나님, with the divine-name setting on 하나님
decisions.reason: Adonai followed by the divine name is 주 with the setting on the second word, so that the default reads 주 하나님 and the alternative 주 야훼, as in the earlier books.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah speaks to God in 합쇼체 with 저
decisions.reason: People address God in 합쇼체 with 저/제, as in the Psalms and the prayers of Kings; this holds for all of Jeremiah's words to God in the book.

decisions.choice: Ah, Senhor DEUS! (L, B); Ah, não, Senhor DEUS! (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 4:10; 14:13; 32:17): the cry of dismay (m2) is "Ah", and Adonai with the divine name is "Senhor DEUS", as the Old Testament terms set it, so that the default never reads "Senhor SENHOR". The vocative takes no "ó", as Isaiah's vocative "SENHOR" takes none. Readable adds "não", as the English Readable says "Oh no".

decisions.choice: um rapaz (L, B); muito novo (R)
decisions.reason: The word covers a boy or young man (m1); "criança" would make Jeremiah a small child, which the text does not say. "Rapaz" says he is young, not yet of an age to be heard.

decisions.choice: "ወይኔ፣ ጌታ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሆይ!" (Literal, Balanced); "ኧረ ጌታ ... ሆይ!" (Readable)
decisions.reason: Adonai YHWH is "ጌታ" followed by the divine name, as in the Pentateuch. The cry of dismay ("ah", also in 4:10 and 14:13) is "ወይኔ", kept apart from "ወዮ", which renders the prophets' "woe" (hoy); Readable uses the everyday "ኧረ". "ብላቴና" (Literal) is a boy or young lad; Balanced and Readable say "ገና ልጅ / ገና ወጣት ነኝ".

decisions.choice: हाय, प्रभु {{divine_name:परमेश्वर|याहवे}}!
decisions.reason: "Lord GOD" (Adonai YHWH) is प्रभु {{divine_name:परमेश्वर|याहवे}}, as the terms note and Psalms have it: प्रभु is the title, and the name inside the span is परमेश्वर so as not to say "प्रभु प्रभु". The cry of dismay is हाय, as Joshua 7:7 and Judges 6:22 have the same words.

decisions.choice: Владыка ГОСПОДИ (vocative)
decisions.reason: Adonai YHWH is Владыка ГОСПОДЬ, as the Prophets note and the Psalms have it, here in the vocative. These are Jeremiah's own words, so his я takes no span.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah speaks to God in です・ます at every level; 'ahah 'adonai YHWH "ああ、{{divine_name:主なる神|主ヤハウェ}}よ" (L, B; R "ああ、とても無理です、…よ" for the English R "Oh no"); hinneh in his words "ご覧ください" (L), dropped (B, R).
decisions.reason: Prose speech to God is polite, as Isaiah 6:8; the cry 'ahah keeps one form through the book (4:10, 14:13, 32:17).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י אַל־תֹּאמַ֖ר נַ֣עַר אָנֹ֑כִי כִּ֠י עַֽל־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֶֽשְׁלָחֲךָ֙ תֵּלֵ֔ךְ וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲצַוְּךָ֖ תְּדַבֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to me, do not say, a youth I [am], for to all whom I send you you will go, and all that I command you you will speak.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Do not say, 'A youth I [am],' for to everyone to whom I send you, you will go, and all that I command you, you will speak.
en.B: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Do not say, 'I am a mere youth.' To all the people I send you to, you will go; every word I command you, you will speak.
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Do not say, 'I am still young.' When I send you to people, you must go. When I give you a message, you must speak it.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «No digas: “Muchacho [soy]”, porque a todos a quienes yo te envíe irás, y todo lo que yo te mande hablarás.
es.B: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «No digas: “No soy más que un muchacho”. Irás a todos aquellos a quienes yo te envíe, y dirás todo lo que yo te mande.
es.R: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «No digas: “Todavía soy muy joven”. Cuando yo te envíe a alguien, tienes que ir. Cuando yo te dé un mensaje, tienes que decirlo.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me dit : « Ne dis pas : “Je [suis] un garçon”, car vers tous ceux vers qui je t’enverrai, tu iras, et tout ce que je te commanderai, tu le diras.
fr.B: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me dit : « Ne dis pas : “Je ne suis qu’un jeune garçon.” Vers tous ceux à qui je t’enverrai, tu iras ; toute parole que je t’ordonnerai, tu la diras.
fr.R: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a dit : « Ne dis pas : “Je suis encore trop jeune.” Quand je t’enverrai vers des gens, tu devras y aller. Quand je te donnerai un message, tu devras le dire.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Usiseme, 'Mimi [ni] kijana,' kwa maana kwa wote nitakaokutuma kwao utakwenda, na yote nitakayokuamuru utayasema.
sw.B: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Usiseme, 'Mimi ni kijana tu.' Utakwenda kwa watu wote nitakaokutuma kwao; kila neno nitakalokuamuru utalisema.
sw.R: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Usiseme, 'Bado mimi ni kijana.' Nikikutuma kwa watu, ni lazima uende. Nikikupa ujumbe, ni lazima uuseme.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với tôi: "Đừng nói: 'Con [là] một đứa trẻ', vì đến với tất cả những ai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai ngươi đi, ngươi sẽ đi, và mọi điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} truyền cho ngươi, ngươi sẽ nói.
vi.B: Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với tôi: "Đừng nói: 'Con chỉ là một đứa trẻ.' Ta sai con đến với ai, con sẽ đi đến với người ấy; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} truyền cho con lời nào, con sẽ nói lời ấy.
vi.R: Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với tôi: "Đừng nói: 'Con còn trẻ quá.' Khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai con đến với ai, con phải đi. Khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ban cho con sứ điệp nào, con phải nói ra.

ko.L: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "'저는 아이입니다' 하고 말하지 마라. 내가 너를 보내는 모든 사람에게 너는 갈 것이고, 내가 너에게 명령하는 모든 것을 너는 말할 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "'저는 아직 어린 젊은이일 뿐입니다' 하고 말하지 마라. 내가 너를 누구에게 보내든지 너는 가야 하고, 내가 너에게 무엇을 명령하든지 너는 그 말을 해야 한다.
ko.R: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "'저는 아직 어립니다' 하고 말하지 마라. 내가 너를 사람들에게 보내면 너는 가야 한다. 내가 너에게 전할 말을 주면 너는 그것을 말해야 한다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me disse: "Não digas: 'Um rapaz eu [sou]', pois a todos aqueles a quem eu te enviar irás, e tudo o que eu te ordenar falarás.
pt.B: Mas {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me disse: "Não digas: 'Sou apenas um rapaz.' Tu irás a todos aqueles a quem eu te enviar e dirás cada palavra que eu te ordenar.
pt.R: Mas {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me disse: "Não digas: 'Ainda sou muito novo.' Quando eu te enviar a alguém, tu deves ir. Quando eu te der uma mensagem, deves anunciá-la.

am.L: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም እንዲህ አለኝ፦ «“ብላቴና ነኝ” አትበል፤ ወደምልክህ ሁሉ ትሄዳለህና፤ የማዝዝህንም ሁሉ ትናገራለህ።
am.B: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ግን እንዲህ አለኝ፦ «“ገና ልጅ ነኝ” አትበል። ወደምልክህ ሰዎች ሁሉ ትሄዳለህ፤ የማዝዝህንም ቃል ሁሉ ትናገራለህ።
am.R: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ግን እንዲህ አለኝ፦ «“ገና ወጣት ነኝ” አትበል። ወደ ሰዎች ስልክህ መሄድ አለብህ። መልእክት ስሰጥህ መናገር አለብህ።

hi.L: और {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने मुझसे कहा, "यह न कहो, 'मैं लड़का [हूँ],' क्योंकि जिन जिनके पास मैं तुम्हें भेजूँ, उन सब के पास तुम जाओगे, और जो कुछ मैं तुम्हें आज्ञा दूँ, वह सब तुम कहोगे।
hi.B: पर {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने मुझसे कहा, "यह मत कहो, 'मैं तो अभी लड़का ही हूँ।' जिन लोगों के पास मैं तुम्हें भेजूँ, उन सब के पास तुम जाओगे; जो भी बात मैं तुम्हें आज्ञा दूँ, वह तुम कहोगे।
hi.R: पर {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने मुझसे कहा, "यह मत कहो, 'मैं अभी कम उम्र का हूँ।' जब मैं तुम्हें लोगों के पास भेजूँ, तब तुम्हें जाना होगा। जब मैं तुम्हें कोई संदेश दूँ, तब तुम्हें उसे सुनाना होगा।

ru.L: И сказал {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} мне: «Не говори: “Юн я”, потому что ко всем, к кому {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} пошлю тебя, ты пойдёшь, и всё, что {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} повелю тебе, ты скажешь.
ru.B: Но {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} сказал мне: «Не говори: “Я ещё слишком молод.” Ко всем, к кому {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} пошлю тебя, ты пойдёшь; каждое слово, которое {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} повелю тебе, ты скажешь.
ru.R: Но {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} сказал мне: «Не говори: “Я ещё молод.” Когда {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} посылаю тебя к людям, ты должен идти. Когда {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} даю тебе слово, ты должен его сказать.

ja.L: すると{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はわたしに言われた。「『わたしは若者です』と言ってはならない。わたしがあなたを遣わすすべての者のところへ、あなたは行き、わたしがあなたに命じるすべてのことを、あなたは語るからだ。
ja.B: しかし{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はわたしに言われた。「『まだほんの若者です』と言ってはならない。わたしが遣わすすべての人のところへ、あなたは行く。わたしが命じる言葉は、すべてあなたが語る。
ja.R: けれども、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はわたしに言われました。「『まだ若いのです』と言ってはいけない。わたしがあなたを人々のところへ遣わすなら、あなたは行かなければならない。わたしがあなたに言葉を与えるなら、あなたはそれを語らなければならない。

decisions.choice: to all to whom I send you: to every person I send you to
alternatives: on every errand I send you
decisions.reason: The phrase can be read as "to all the people to whom I send you" or as "on every errand I send you". Both say that God's sending, not Jeremiah's age, decides where he goes.

decisions.choice: all that I command you: the prophet's authority rests on God's command
decisions.reason: God does not deny that Jeremiah is young. He answers that the message and the sending are his, as he told Moses (Exodus 4:11-12; Deuteronomy 18:18).

decisions.choice: When I send you to people, you must go. When I give you a message, you must speak it.
decisions.reason: Readable turns the two long clauses into short sentences with the same sense.

decisions.choice: God's commands and prohibitions to the prophet in the prose narrative: "〜なさい" (L, B), "〜しなさい" (R); prohibitions "〜してはならない" (L, B), "〜してはいけない" (R). In the verse oracles the oracle forms hold ("〜せよ" / "〜するな" at Literal).
decisions.reason: As Kings and Isaiah 7:3: the narrative forms for God's instructions inside a story.

records.literal_gloss: Do not be afraid of their faces, for with you I [am] to deliver you, declares Yahweh.

en.L: Do not be afraid of their faces, for with you I [am] to deliver you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: Have no fear of them, for I am with you to rescue you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: Do not be afraid of them. I am with you, and I will keep you safe, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

es.L: No temas delante de sus rostros, porque contigo [estoy] yo para librarte, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}».
es.B: No les tengas miedo, porque yo estoy contigo para rescatarte, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}».
es.R: No les tengas miedo. Yo estoy contigo y te protegeré, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}».

fr.L: N’aie pas peur de leurs faces, car avec toi je [suis] pour te délivrer, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. »
fr.B: N’aie aucune crainte devant eux, car je suis avec toi pour te délivrer, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. »
fr.R: N’aie pas peur d’eux. Je suis avec toi et je te protégerai, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. »

sw.L: Usiogope nyuso zao, kwa maana pamoja nawe mimi [niko] kukuokoa, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.B: Usiwaogope, kwa maana niko pamoja nawe ili nikuokoe, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.R: Usiwaogope. Niko pamoja nawe, nami nitakulinda salama, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."

vi.L: Đừng sợ mặt chúng, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở với ngươi để giải cứu ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy."
vi.B: Đừng sợ chúng, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở với con để cứu con, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy."
vi.R: Đừng sợ họ. Ta ở với con, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ giữ con được an toàn, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán."

ko.L: 그들의 얼굴을 두려워하지 마라. 내가 너와 함께 있어 너를 건져 낼 것이기 때문이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다."
ko.B: 그들을 두려워하지 마라. 내가 너와 함께 있으면서 너를 구해 낼 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다."
ko.R: 그들을 무서워하지 마라. 내가 너와 함께 있으면서 너를 지켜 주겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다."

pt.L: Não tenhas medo do rosto deles, pois contigo eu [estou] para te livrar, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}."
pt.B: Não tenhas medo deles, pois eu estou contigo para te resgatar, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}."
pt.R: Não tenhas medo deles. Eu estou contigo e vou te proteger, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}."

am.L: ከፊታቸው አትፍራ፤ ላድንህ ከአንተ ጋር ነኝና፤ ይላል {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}።»
am.B: አትፍራቸው፤ ልታደግህ ከአንተ ጋር ነኝና፤ ይላል {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}።»
am.R: አትፍራቸው። እኔ ከአንተ ጋር ነኝ፤ ከክፉም እጠብቅሃለሁ፤ ይላል {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}።»

hi.L: उनके चेहरों से न डरो, क्योंकि तुम्हें छुड़ाने के लिए मैं तुम्हारे साथ [हूँ], {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की यह वाणी है।"
hi.B: उनसे मत डरो, क्योंकि तुम्हें छुड़ाने के लिए मैं तुम्हारे साथ हूँ, {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की यह वाणी है।"
hi.R: उनसे मत डरना। मैं तुम्हारे साथ हूँ, और मैं तुम्हें सुरक्षित रखूँगा, {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} कहते हैं।"

ru.L: Не бойся их лиц, потому что с тобой {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}}, чтобы избавлять тебя, — слово {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}.»
ru.B: Не бойся их, потому что {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} с тобой, чтобы избавить тебя, — говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}.»
ru.R: Не бойся их. Я с тобой, и {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} сохраню тебя, — говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}.»

ja.L: 彼らの顔を恐れてはならない。わたしがあなたと共にいて、あなたを救い出すからだ。――{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の言葉――」
ja.B: 彼らを恐れてはならない。わたしがあなたと共にいて、あなたを助け出すからだ、と{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は告げる。」
ja.R: 彼らを怖がってはいけない。わたしはあなたと一緒にいて、あなたを守る、と{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は言う。」

decisions.choice: afraid of their faces: afraid of them, afraid to face them
decisions.reason: "Face" here stands for the people themselves as they confront the prophet. They are the people to whom he is sent (verse 7), named in verse 18.

decisions.choice: I am with you: God's promise of his presence to the one he sends
decisions.reason: God made the same promise to Isaac (Genesis 26:3), Moses (Exodus 3:12) and Gideon (Judges 6:16). It returns at the end of the chapter (verse 19), framing the whole call.

decisions.choice: declares Yahweh: a formula marking the words as Yahweh's own
decisions.reason: The noun means "an utterance"; the formula seals what precedes as the LORD's own declaration. It is very frequent in Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: rescue (Balanced); keep you safe (Readable); deliver (Literal)
decisions.reason: The verb means to snatch someone out of danger. The same wording is used in verse 19.

decisions.choice: "declara el SEÑOR" (L); "afirma el SEÑOR" (B); "dice el SEÑOR" (R)
decisions.reason: The formula ne'um YHWH as the terms note sets it for Spanish, after a comma, at every use in Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: asema BWANA (Literal, Balanced); anasema BWANA (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording of the formula ne'um YHWH, as in 2 Kings 19:33 and the terms note; Readable uses the everyday present.

decisions.choice: ili nikuokoe (Balanced); nitakulinda salama (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb is to snatch out of danger; Readable says plainly that God will keep him safe, as the English Readable. Verse 19 repeats the same wording.

decisions.choice: "déclare le SEIGNEUR" (L, B); "dit le SEIGNEUR" (R), for the whole book
decisions.reason: The formula seals the words as the LORD's own (m3); "déclare" keeps it a verb, as 2 Kings 19:33 and 22:19 do, and Readable uses the plainest verb.

decisions.choice: "CHÚA phán vậy" (Literal, Balanced); "CHÚA phán" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The terms note's form for "declares the LORD" (neʾum YHWH), as 2 Kings 9:26, kept through the book.

decisions.choice: 주의 선언이다 (Literal); 주가 말한다 (Balanced, Readable), each as its own sentence
decisions.reason: The formula is very frequent in Jeremiah and keeps one wording at each level. Korean cannot place it inside a sentence, so it closes the clause as its own short sentence. In God's own mouth it takes no honorific -시-, since God names himself.

decisions.choice: declara o SENHOR (L, B); diz o SENHOR (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: ne'um, the formula that seals words as the LORD's own (m3), takes the wording Isaiah 1:24 sets in Portuguese: "declara" at Literal and Balanced, "diz" at Readable, as the English. The other prophetic formulas follow Isaiah too: "Assim diz o SENHOR" (L, B) / "É isto que o SENHOR diz" (R) for koh 'amar (Isaiah 7:7), "eis que" (L) for hinneh (Isaiah 3:1), "Ai de" for hoy (Isaiah 1:4), "o SENHOR dos Exércitos" (Isaiah 1:9), "naquele dia" (Isaiah 2:11).

decisions.choice: livrar (L); resgatar (B); proteger (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to snatch someone out of danger; the three levels keep the English's distinction, and verse 19 repeats each word.

decisions.choice: "ይላል {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}" after the words it marks, at every level
decisions.reason: The formula "declares the LORD" (neʾum YHWH) follows the words it seals, with the verb first ("ይላል {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}"), as in 2 Kings 19:33 on main; it stays apart from "Thus says the LORD", which comes before the speech ("{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዲህ ይላል"). Readable, whose English says "says", uses the same Amharic, which already means both.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की यह वाणी है (L, B); {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} कहते हैं (R)
decisions.reason: The formula ne'um YHWH ("declares the LORD") has one wording per level through the Prophets, as the terms note sets it and Isaiah has it; it stands where the Hebrew has it, inside the sentence or at its end. Book-wide choice for Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: — слово ГОСПОДА (L); — говорит ГОСПОДЬ (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Prophets note's wording for neum YHWH, kept every time in Jeremiah. Literal keeps the Hebrew noun ("utterance"); Balanced and Readable use the verb.

decisions.choice: ne'um YHWH "――{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の言葉――" (L), "と{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は告げる" (B), "と{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は言う" (R), as Isaiah; hatsil "救い出す" (L), "助け出す" (B), "守る" (R, as the English R "keep you safe"); the promise of 1:19 has the same words.
decisions.reason: The prophetic formula table; 1:8 and 1:19 are worded alike so the repeated promise is heard.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ אֶת־יָד֔וֹ וַיַּגַּ֖ע עַל־פִּ֑י וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י הִנֵּ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי דְבָרַ֖י בְּפִֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And stretched out Yahweh his hand and made touch on my mouth, and said Yahweh to me, look, I have put my words in your mouth.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stretched out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and made [it] touch my mouth, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Look, I have put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words in your mouth.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} then stretched out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and laid it on my mouth, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "There: I have placed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words in your mouth.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} reached out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and touched my mouth. He said to me, "Now {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words are in your mouth. I have put them there.

es.L: Y extendió {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano y [la] hizo tocar mi boca, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «Mira, he puesto {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras en tu boca.
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} extendió {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano y me tocó la boca, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «Ahí está: he puesto {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras en tu boca.
es.R: Luego {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} extendió {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano y me tocó la boca. Me dijo: «Ahora {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras están en tu boca. Yo las he puesto allí.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} étendit {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main et [la] fit toucher ma bouche, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me dit : « Voici, j’ai mis {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles dans ta bouche.
fr.B: Puis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} étendit {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main et la posa sur ma bouche, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me dit : « Voilà, j’ai placé {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles dans ta bouche.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a tendu {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main et a touché ma bouche. Il m’a dit : « Maintenant, {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles sont dans ta bouche. Je les y ai mises.

sw.L: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akanyosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akaufanya [mkono] uguse kinywa changu, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Tazama, nimeweka maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kinywani mwako.
sw.B: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akanyosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} akakigusa kinywa changu, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Basi, nimeyaweka maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kinywani mwako.
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akanyosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} akakigusa kinywa changu. Akaniambia, "Sasa maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} yamo kinywani mwako. Mimi nimeyaweka humo.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giơ tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ra và chạm vào miệng tôi, rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với tôi: "Kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đặt lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trong miệng ngươi.
vi.B: Rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đưa tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ra đặt trên miệng tôi, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với tôi: "Đây, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đặt lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trong miệng con.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 손을 내미셔서 [그것을] 내 입에 대시고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "보아라, 내가 내 말들을 네 입에 두었다.
ko.B: 그런 다음 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 손을 뻗어 내 입에 대시고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "자, 내가 내 말을 네 입에 넣어 주었다.
ko.R: 그러고 나서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 손을 내밀어 내 입을 만지시고 나에게 말씀하셨다. "이제 내 말이 네 입에 있다. 내가 그것을 거기에 넣어 주었다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} estendeu a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão e [a] fez tocar a minha boca, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me disse: "Eis que pus as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras na tua boca.
pt.B: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} estendeu a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão e a pôs sobre a minha boca, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me disse: "Pronto: coloquei as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras na tua boca.
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} estendeu a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão e tocou a minha boca. Ele me disse: "Agora as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras estão na tua boca. Eu as coloquei aí.

am.L: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም እጁን ዘረጋ፤ በአፌም ላይ አስነካ፤ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም እንዲህ አለኝ፦ «እነሆ፣ ቃሎቼን በአፍህ አኖርኩ።
am.B: ከዚያም {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እጁን ዘርግቶ በአፌ ላይ አደረገ፤ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም እንዲህ አለኝ፦ «ይኸው፣ ቃሎቼን በአፍህ አኑሬአለሁ።
am.R: ከዚያም {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እጁን ዘርግቶ አፌን ነካ። እንዲህም አለኝ፦ «አሁን ቃሎቼ በአፍህ ውስጥ ናቸው። እኔ አስቀምጫቸዋለሁ።

hi.B: तब {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने अपना हाथ बढ़ाकर मेरे मुँह पर रखा, और {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने मुझसे कहा, "लो, मैंने अपने वचन तुम्हारे मुँह में रख दिए हैं।

ru.L: И простёр {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} свою руку и коснулся [ею] моих уст, и сказал {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} мне: «Вот, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} вложил {{deity_pronoun:мои|Мои}} слова в твои уста.
ru.B: Тогда {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} протянул руку и прикоснулся к моим устам, и {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} сказал мне: «Вот: {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} вложил {{deity_pronoun:мои|Мои}} слова в твои уста.
ru.R: Потом {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} протянул руку и коснулся моих губ. Он сказал мне: «Теперь {{deity_pronoun:мои|Мои}} слова в твоих устах. Я вложил их туда.

ja.L: そして{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はその手を伸ばして、わたしの口に触れさせ、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はわたしに言われた。「見なさい、わたしはわたしの言葉をあなたの口に置いた。
ja.B: それから{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は手を伸ばして、わたしの口に触れ、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はわたしに言われた。「さあ、わたしはわたしの言葉をあなたの口に授けた。
ja.R: それから、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は手を伸ばして、わたしの口に触れられました。そして、わたしに言われました。「今、わたしの言葉はあなたの口の中にある。わたしがそこに置いたのだ。

decisions.choice: touched my mouth: a sign that God himself prepares the prophet to speak
decisions.reason: Isaiah's lips were touched with a coal from the altar (Isaiah 6:7), and Ezekiel was given a scroll to eat (Ezekiel 3:1-3). Here the LORD's own hand touches Jeremiah's mouth, answering his fear that he cannot speak (verse 6).

decisions.choice: I have put my words in your mouth: the promise of a prophet like Moses
decisions.reason: God promised to raise up a prophet like Moses and said, "I will put my words in his mouth" (Deuteronomy 18:18). Jeremiah is that kind of prophet: he will speak only what God gives him (5:14; 15:19).

decisions.choice: I have put: done now, in this very act
decisions.reason: The verb describes what God does as he speaks. From this moment Jeremiah's words are God's words.

decisions.choice: Look (Literal); There (Balanced); Now (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word points to what has just happened. Balanced and Readable choose words that point to the moment of the touch.

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns for God inside the verb ("akaniambia", "nimeyaweka"), and a verb prefix cannot take a capital, so the deity_pronoun span stands only on the free pronouns and possessives ("mkono wake", "maneno yangu"); Swahili therefore has fewer spans than the English in this book.

decisions.choice: "Voici" (L); "Voilà" (B); "Maintenant" (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable point to the moment of the touch, as the English does.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: deity_pronoun spans as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change. Respect for God is carried by -시- and 께서 (손을 내미셔서, 말씀하셨다), at every level, throughout the book.

decisions.choice: Eis que (L); Pronto (B); Agora (R)
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1): Literal keeps "eis que" for hinneh, Balanced and Readable point to the moment of the touch, "Pronto" being the Portuguese word for something just done.

decisions.choice: hinneh in God's words "見なさい" (L), "さあ" (B, as the English B "There"), "今" (R); never "見よ".
decisions.reason: The prophetic convention for hinneh, with Balanced and Readable following the English per level.

records.literal_gloss: See, I have appointed you the day this over the nations and over the kingdoms, to uproot and to tear down and to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant.

en.L: See, I have appointed you this day over the nations and over the kingdoms, \q to uproot and to tear down, and to destroy and to overthrow, \q to build and to plant."
en.B: See, on this day I have set you over nations and over kingdoms, \q to uproot and to tear down, to destroy and overthrow, \q to build and plant."
en.R: Look! Today I am giving you authority over nations and kingdoms. \q You will uproot and tear down, destroy and overthrow. \q You will build and plant."

es.L: Mira, te he puesto en este día sobre las naciones y sobre los reinos, \q para arrancar y para derribar, y para destruir y para derrocar, \q para edificar y para plantar».
es.B: Mira, en este día te he puesto sobre naciones y sobre reinos, \q para arrancar y derribar, para destruir y derrocar, \q para edificar y plantar».
es.R: ¡Mira! Hoy te doy autoridad sobre naciones y reinos. \q Arrancarás y derribarás, destruirás y derrocarás. \q Edificarás y plantarás».

fr.L: Vois, je t’ai établi en ce jour sur les nations et sur les royaumes, \q pour arracher et pour démolir, et pour détruire et pour renverser, \q pour bâtir et pour planter. »

fr.R: Regarde ! Aujourd’hui, je te donne autorité sur les nations et les royaumes. \q Tu arracheras et tu démoliras, tu détruiras et tu renverseras. \q Tu bâtiras et tu planteras. »

sw.L: Tazama, nimekuweka leo hii juu ya mataifa na juu ya falme, \q kung'oa na kubomoa, na kuangamiza na kuangusha, \q kujenga na kupanda."

decisions.choice: uproot, tear down, destroy, overthrow, build, plant: four words of judgment and two of restoration
decisions.reason: The pictures come from farming and building: plants pulled up and buildings pulled down, then buildings put up and trees planted. Judgment comes first and takes up most of the line, but the last word is building and planting. The pairs return through the book (18:7-9; 24:6; 31:28; 42:10; 45:4).

decisions.choice: appointed you over the nations: authority exercised through the word God has given
decisions.reason: The verb means to put someone in charge. Jeremiah holds no throne or army; he uproots and builds by speaking the word God put in his mouth (verse 9), and God carries it out (verse 12).

decisions.choice: uproot, tear down, destroy, overthrow, build, plant
decisions.reason: Each level keeps these six English verbs wherever the list or part of it returns in Jeremiah, so the reader can hear the echo of this verse.

decisions.choice: giving you authority ... You will
decisions.reason: Readable says what being set over the nations means and turns the purpose clauses into plain statements of what Jeremiah will do.

decisions.choice: to uproot and to tear down, to destroy and overthrow, to build and plant
decisions.reason: Balanced drops the repeated "to" in the last two pairs, as natural English lists do. The six verbs and their order stay the same (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: "arrancar, derribar, destruir, derrocar, edificar, plantar"
decisions.reason: Each level keeps these six Spanish verbs wherever the list or part of it returns in Jeremiah (18:7-9; 24:6; 31:28; 42:10; 45:4), so the echo of this verse can be heard.

decisions.choice: kung'oa, kubomoa, kuangamiza, kuangusha, kujenga, kupanda
decisions.reason: Each level keeps these six Swahili verbs wherever the list or part of it returns in Jeremiah (18:7-9; 24:6; 31:28; 42:10; 45:4), as the English does.

decisions.choice: "arracher, démolir, détruire, renverser, bâtir, planter"
decisions.reason: Each level keeps these six French verbs wherever the list or part of it returns in Jeremiah (18:7-9; 24:6; 31:28; 42:10; 45:4), so the reader hears the echo of this verse.

decisions.reason: The six verbs are kept at each level wherever the list or part of it returns in Jeremiah (12:14-17; 18:7-9; 24:6; 31:28; 42:10; 45:4), so the echo of this verse can be heard.

decisions.choice: 뽑다, 허물다, 멸하다, 무너뜨리다, 세우다, 심다
decisions.reason: Each level keeps these six verbs wherever the list or part of it returns in Jeremiah (18:7-9; 24:6; 31:28; 42:10; 45:4), so the echo of this verse can be heard.

decisions.choice: arrancar, derrubar, destruir, arrasar, construir, plantar

"Construir" is the everyday verb for building and pairs with "plantar" in plain Portuguese; "arrasar" is the verb for leveling a city or a wall.

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying, what [are] you seeing, Jeremiah? And I said, a rod of almond I [am] seeing.

en.L: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying: "What [are] you seeing, Jeremiah?" And I said, "A rod of almond I [am] seeing."
en.B: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me: "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I said, "I see a rod cut from an almond tree."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message: "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I answered, "I see a stick from an almond tree."

es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dio este mensaje: «¿Qué ves, Jeremías?». Yo respondí: «Veo una rama cortada de un almendro».

fr.B: La parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} me fut adressée : « Que vois-tu, Jérémie ? » Je répondis : « Je vois une baguette coupée sur un amandier. »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a donné ce message : « Que vois-tu, Jérémie ? » J’ai répondu : « Je vois un bâton d’amandier. »

sw.L: Neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} likanijia, kusema: "Unaona nini, Yeremia?" Nami nikasema, "Fimbo ya mlozi ninaiona."
sw.B: Neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} likanijia: "Unaona nini, Yeremia?" Nikasema, "Ninaona fimbo iliyokatwa kutoka mti wa mlozi."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alinipa ujumbe huu: "Unaona nini, Yeremia?" Nikajibu, "Ninaona kijiti cha mti wa mlozi."

vi.L: Lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với tôi rằng: "Giê-rê-mi, ngươi đang thấy gì?" Tôi nói: "Con đang thấy một cành hạnh."
vi.B: Lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với tôi: "Giê-rê-mi, con thấy gì?" Tôi thưa: "Con thấy một cây gậy cắt từ cây hạnh."
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho tôi sứ điệp này: "Giê-rê-mi, con thấy gì?" Tôi đáp: "Con thấy một cành gậy lấy từ cây hạnh."

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 나에게 임하여 말씀하셨다. "예레미야야, 너는 무엇을 보고 있느냐?" 그래서 내가 말했다. "아몬드나무 막대기를 제가 보고 있습니다."
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 나에게 임했다. "예레미야야, 무엇이 보이느냐?" 내가 말했다. "아몬드나무에서 꺾은 막대기가 보입니다."
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 이 말씀을 주셨다. "예레미야야, 무엇이 보이느냐?" 내가 대답했다. "아몬드나무로 만든 막대기가 보입니다."

pt.L: E a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a mim, dizendo: "O que tu [estás] vendo, Jeremias?" E eu disse: "Uma vara de amendoeira eu [estou] vendo."
pt.B: A palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a mim: "O que vês, Jeremias?" Eu disse: "Vejo uma vara cortada de uma amendoeira."
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} me deu esta mensagem: "O que estás vendo, Jeremias?" Eu respondi: "Vejo uma vara tirada de uma amendoeira."

am.L: {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ቃል ወደ እኔ መጣ፤ እንዲህም አለ፦ «ኤርምያስ ሆይ፣ ምን ታያለህ?» እኔም እንዲህ አልኩ፦ «የለውዝ በትር አያለሁ።»
am.B: {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ቃል ወደ እኔ መጣ፦ «ኤርምያስ ሆይ፣ ምን ታያለህ?» እኔም እንዲህ አልኩ፦ «ከለውዝ ዛፍ የተቆረጠ በትር አያለሁ።»
am.R: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ይህን መልእክት ሰጠኝ፦ «ኤርምያስ ሆይ፣ ምን ታያለህ?» እኔም እንዲህ ብዬ መለስኩ፦ «ከለውዝ ዛፍ የተቆረጠ ዱላ አያለሁ።»

hi.L: और {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} का वचन मेरे पास पहुँचा: "यिर्मयाह, तुम क्या देख रहे हो?" और मैंने कहा, "मैं बादाम की एक छड़ी देख रहा हूँ।"
hi.B: {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} का वचन मेरे पास पहुँचा: "यिर्मयाह, तुम्हें क्या दिखाई देता है?" मैंने कहा, "मुझे बादाम के पेड़ से काटी हुई एक छड़ी दिखाई देती है।"
hi.R: {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने मुझे यह संदेश दिया: "यिर्मयाह, तुम्हें क्या दिखाई देता है?" मैंने उत्तर दिया, "मुझे बादाम के पेड़ की एक छड़ी दिखाई देती है।"

ru.L: И было слово {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}} ко мне, говоря: «Что ты видишь, Иеремия?» И сказал я: «Миндальный прут я вижу.»
ru.B: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} обратился ко мне: «Что ты видишь, Иеремия?» Я сказал: «Я вижу прут, срезанный с миндального дерева.»
ru.R: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} дал мне такое слово: «Что ты видишь, Иеремия?» Я ответил: «Я вижу палку от миндального дерева.»

ja.L: そして{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の言葉がわたしに臨んで言った。「エレミヤよ、あなたは何を見ているか？」わたしは言った。「アーモンドの枝を、わたしは見ています。」
ja.B: {{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の言葉がわたしに臨んだ。「エレミヤよ、何が見えるか？」わたしは言った。「アーモンドの木から切った枝が見えます。」
ja.R: {{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は、わたしに次のように語られました。「エレミヤよ、何が見えるか？」わたしは答えました。「アーモンドの木の枝が見えます。」

decisions.choice: a rod: a stick or staff cut from a tree
decisions.reason: The word means a stick, rod or staff (Genesis 30:37; Numbers 22:27; 1 Samuel 17:40). Nothing is said of buds or blossoms; what matters is the name of the tree (verse 12).

decisions.choice: almond: the tree that wakes first
decisions.reason: The almond is the first tree in the land to blossom, in late winter, while other trees still look dead. Aaron's staff, which sprouted overnight, bore almonds (Numbers 17:23). Its name sounds like the word for "watching" (see verse 12).

decisions.choice: What do you see?: a vision explained by God's question and answer
decisions.reason: God asks the prophet to name what he sees and then explains it, as he does with Amos (Amos 7:8; 8:2) and later with Jeremiah (24:3).

decisions.choice: a rod cut from an almond tree (Balanced); a stick from an almond tree (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that this is a cut stick, not a living branch on the tree.

decisions.choice: "Je vois une baguette d’amandier"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts the object first; French cannot without an echoing pronoun, so Literal uses the normal order.

decisions.choice: "cây hạnh" (almond tree)
decisions.reason: "Hạnh" is the short name of the almond tree used for Aaron's rod (Numbers 17:23). Balanced and Readable say the rod was cut from the tree, as the English does.

decisions.choice: 아몬드나무
decisions.reason: The tree is the almond, the first to blossom in late winter; older Korean Bibles call it 살구나무 (apricot). The modern name is used so the reader can follow the picture of verse 12.

decisions.choice: uma vara de amendoeira
decisions.reason: The word is a cut stick or rod (m1), not a living branch, so every level says "vara"; "ramo" would suggest a branch in bloom, which the text does not mention.

decisions.choice: "ለውዝ" for the almond tree
decisions.reason: "ለውዝ" is the word Amharic Bibles have used for the almond, though in everyday speech it often means the peanut; Balanced and Readable say "ከለውዝ ዛፍ" (from an almond tree) so a tree is meant. A reviewer may prefer the loanword.

decisions.choice: बादाम की एक छड़ी (L); बादाम के पेड़ से काटी हुई एक छड़ी (B)
decisions.reason: maqqel is a rod or stick cut from a tree, not a living branch, so छड़ी rather than डाली; Balanced says it was cut, as the English does. बादाम is the almond, a tree known in India by the same name.

decisions.choice: миндальный прут (L); прут, срезанный с миндального дерева (B); палка от миндального дерева (R)
decisions.reason: A cut stick, not a branch on the tree (meaning m1), in plain words rather than the Synodal "жезл". The almond matters for the wordplay of verse 12.

decisions.choice: maqqel shaqed "アーモンドの枝" (L), "アーモンドの木から切った枝" (B), "アーモンドの木の枝" (R); Jeremiah answers politely ("見えます").
decisions.reason: The wordplay with "見張る" in 1:12 cannot be heard in Japanese; the footnote of 1:12 explains it, and the Readable says it in the text as the English Readable does.

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to me, you have done well to see, for watching I [am] over my word to do it.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "You have done well to see, for watching I [am] over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word to do it."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "You have seen rightly, for I am keeping watch over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word until I carry it out."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "You are right. The name of the almond tree sounds like the word for 'watching.' And I am watching over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word to make sure it comes true."

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «Bien has visto, porque vigilante [estoy] yo sobre {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} palabra para cumplirla».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «Has visto bien, porque yo estoy vigilando {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} palabra hasta cumplirla».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «Tienes razón. En hebreo, el nombre del almendro suena como la palabra “vigilante”. Y yo estoy vigilando {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} palabra para que se cumpla».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me dit : « Tu as bien vu, car je veille sur {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} parole pour l’accomplir. »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me dit : « Tu as bien vu, car je veille sur {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} parole jusqu’à ce que je l’accomplisse. »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a dit : « Tu as raison. Le nom de l’amandier ressemble au mot qui veut dire “veiller”. Et je veille sur {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} parole pour qu’elle se réalise. »

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Umefanya vema kuona, kwa maana ninakesha juu ya neno {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} kulitenda."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Umeona sawasawa, kwa maana ninakesha nikililinda neno {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} mpaka nitakapolitimiza."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Uko sahihi. Kwa Kiebrania jina la mlozi linasikika kama neno la 'kukesha.' Nami ninakesha nikililinda neno {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} ili kuhakikisha linatimia."

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với tôi: "Ngươi đã thấy đúng, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang canh thức trên lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} để thực hiện nó."
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với tôi: "Con thấy đúng lắm, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang canh giữ lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cho đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thực hiện."
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với tôi: "Con nói đúng. Trong tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ, tên cây hạnh nghe giống chữ 'canh thức'. Ta đang canh thức trên lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} để chắc chắn lời ấy sẽ thành sự thật."

ko.L: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "네가 잘 보았다. 내가 내 말을 지켜보고 있다가 그것을 이룰 것이기 때문이다."
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "네가 바로 보았다. 나는 내 말이 이루어질 때까지 그것을 지켜보고 있다."
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "네 말이 맞다. 아몬드나무의 이름은 '지켜본다'는 말과 소리가 비슷하다. 나는 내 말이 꼭 이루어지도록 지켜보고 있다."

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me disse: "Fizeste bem em ver, pois vigiando eu [estou] sobre a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} palavra para cumpri-la."
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} me disse: "Viste bem, pois eu estou vigiando a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} palavra até cumpri-la."
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} me disse: "Estás certo. Em hebraico, o nome da amendoeira soa como a palavra 'vigiando'. E eu estou vigiando a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} palavra para garantir que ela se cumpra."

am.L: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም እንዲህ አለኝ፦ «መልካም አየህ፤ ቃሌን ልፈጽመው እኔ እተጋበታለሁና።»
am.B: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዲህ አለኝ፦ «በትክክል አይተሃል፤ ቃሌን እስክፈጽመው ድረስ እጠብቀዋለሁና።»
am.R: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዲህ አለኝ፦ «ትክክል ነህ። በዕብራይስጥ የለውዝ ዛፍ ስም “መጠበቅ” ከሚለው ቃል ጋር ይመሳሰላል። እኔም ቃሌ እንዲፈጸም እጠብቀዋለሁ።»

hi.L: और {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने मुझसे कहा, "तुमने ठीक देखा है, क्योंकि मैं अपने वचन पर जागता [रहता] हूँ कि उसे पूरा करूँ।"
hi.B: {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने मुझसे कहा, "तुमने ठीक देखा है, क्योंकि मैं अपने वचन पर जागकर पहरा दे रहा हूँ, जब तक उसे पूरा न कर दूँ।"
hi.R: {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने मुझसे कहा, "तुम ठीक कहते हो। बादाम के पेड़ का नाम 'जागते रहना' शब्द जैसा सुनाई देता है। और मैं अपने वचन पर जागकर नज़र रख रहा हूँ, ताकि वह ज़रूर पूरा हो।"
